title: You don’t wake up one day and decide to quit God.
paragraphs: You don’t wake up one day and decide to quit God.
It happens slowly.
Quietly.

A prayer you skip.
A compromise you excuse.
A fire that fades into routine.
And suddenly… you’re still showing up, but your heart isn’t.
That’s the danger no one talks about.

Not loud rebellion.
But silent exhaustion.

Galatians 6:9 doesn’t shout—it pleads:
“And let us not grow weary in doing good, for in due season we will reap, if we do not give up.”

That word weary?
It’s not just tired.

It means worn down. Drained. Spiritually fatigued.
The kind of tired that makes you question if obedience is even worth it.

Because you’ve been doing the right thing…
But nothing seems to be changing.

You’ve been praying…
But heaven feels quiet.

You’ve been resisting temptation…
But the battle feels the same.

You’ve been sowing good seeds…
But the ground looks empty.
And here’s where most people fall.

Not into sin first—
But into discouragement.

Because discouragement whispers something dangerous:
“Maybe this isn’t working.”
But here’s what we miss…
The Kingdom of God is a seed story.

Jesus said in Mark 4:26–27:
“The kingdom of God is as if a man should scatter seed on the ground… and the seed sprouts and grows; he knows not how.”
Read that again.
He knows not how.
That means growth is happening—even when you don’t see it.
Even when you don’t feel it.
Even when everything looks the same.
Because God does His deepest work underground.

In hidden places.
In quiet obedience.
In unseen faithfulness.
And the enemy knows this.
So he doesn’t always try to destroy you.
He just tries to make you stop.

Stop praying.
Stop believing.
Stop showing up.
Stop planting.

Because if he can get you to quit—
He doesn’t need to steal your harvest.
You’ll walk away from it yourself.
But listen…
The cross proves something eternal.
Jesus did not quit.

In the garden, He felt the weight.
In Luke 22:42 He prayed,
“Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
That’s consistency.

Not emotional hype.
Not perfect strength.
But surrendered obedience.
All the way to the cross.

Hebrews 12:2 says,
“For the joy that was set before Him, He endured the cross, despising the shame…”
Did you catch that?
He endured.

He didn’t escape.
He didn’t delay.
He didn’t quit.

And because He stayed…
We are saved.

Because He endured…
We have hope.

Because He finished…
We can keep going.

So when Galatians 6:9 tells you not to give up—
It’s not a motivational quote.
It’s a Gospel invitation.
You’re not holding yourself together.
Jesus is.

Your consistency is not powered by your strength—
It’s sustained by His grace.

2 Corinthians 12:9 says,
“My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.”

So even when you feel weak…
You are not disqualified.
You are positioned for His power.
Let that sink in.

Your tired prayers still matter.
Your quiet obedience still counts.
Your unseen faithfulness is still seen by God.

Hebrews 6:10 says,
“God is not unjust; He will not forget your work and the love you have shown Him…”
Not forgotten.
Not wasted.
Not ignored.
There is a harvest coming.

Not because you are perfect—
But because God is faithful.
So don’t measure your life by visible results.
Measure it by obedience.
By surrender.
By staying.
Even when it’s hard.
Even when it’s slow.
Even when no one claps.
Because heaven sees what the world overlooks.

And in Christ…
Your “small” faithfulness is never small.
It is eternal.

So if you’re tired today—
Good.
That means you’re in the fight.

If you’re weary—
Good.
That means you’ve been sowing.

If you feel like quitting—
Pause.
Look at the cross.
He didn’t quit on you.
So don’t walk away from what God is growing in you.
Stay planted.
Stay surrendered.
Stay with Jesus.
Your due season is not a myth.
It’s a promise.
And God does not lie.

Numbers 23:19 says,
“God is not man, that He should lie… Has He said, and will He not do it?”
He will.
He always does.

Because one day—
What you kept showing up for…
Will finally break through.

And when it does—
You’ll realize…
God was working the whole time.
